extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and evidentiary standards for obtaining/assigning USPTO filing dates based on Certificates of Mailing, Certificate practice under 37 CFR 1.8, and Express Mail deposit dates under 37 CFR 1.10 (including petition processes under 1.10(c)-(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness when deadline falls on weekend/holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: If an action in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia (37 CFR 1.7), the action will be considered to be timely if deposited in the United States mail or transmitted by facsimile and certified under 37 CFR 1.8(a) on the next succeeding day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes facsimile and mail deposit certified under 37 CFR 1.8. Also, 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3) was amended to extend the period of pendency of a provisional application to the next succeeding business day if the 12-month anniversary falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C.; applies to provisionals filed on/after June 8, 1995. See 37 CFR 1.7 and 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of continuation/division filings from certificate practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a paper for the purpose of obtaining a continuation or division application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (available only for design applications) is excluded from the Certificate practice under 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2)(i)(A) since it is considered to be the filing of a national patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings are treated as national patent application filings and do not get the certificate-of-mailing benefits under 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2)(i)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Certificate-of-Mailing benefit for establishing new-application filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: No benefit will be given to a Certificate of Mailing or Transmission relative to the filing of a national patent application specification and drawing or other correspondence for the purpose of obtaining an application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New patent applications filed under 37 CFR 1.10 will be stamped with the USPS date of deposit as 'Express Mail' where applicable; but Certificates of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 do not serve to establish a new application filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of Certificates of Mailing/Transmission in file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: All Certificates of Mailing or Transmission filed in applications should be placed in the file wrappers directly below the papers to which they refer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, follow IFW Manual instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling hand-delivered papers claiming mailing benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel receiving a hand-delivered paper from other than U.S. Postal Service personnel should inspect the paper to ensure that the benefits of 37 CFR 1.8 or 'Express Mail' benefits under 37 CFR 1.10 are not accorded in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the paper contains a certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or an 'Express Mail' mailing label, the words 'HAND DELIVERED' should be written adjacent to the date stamp. Applicant should be notified in the next Office action when a paper containing a Certificate of Mailing has been denied the benefits under 37 CFR 1.8 or an 'Express Mail' label is denied benefits under 37 CFR 1.10 (e.g., form paragraph 5.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting misuse or repeated improper claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of a Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or improperly claiming the benefit of 37 CFR 1.10 which appears to be more than a one-time, inadvertent error should be brought to the attention of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated or non-inadvertent misuse may warrant disciplinary review; single inadvertent errors are not necessarily reported but see guidance on due care and petitions/waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when mailed paper was timely deposited but not received (37 CFR 1.8(b)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.8(b) permits a party to notify the Office of a previous mailing, or transmitting, of correspondence when a reasonable amount of time has elapsed from the time of mailing or transmitting and the correspondence was not received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may notify the Office, supply a duplicate copy, and file a statement attesting on personal knowledge or to the satisfaction of the Director to the previous timely mailing or transmission. If the signer did not sign the certificate of mailing, the signer should explain firsthand knowledge. The statement should be filed promptly after awareness of non-receipt. The statement required by 37 CFR 1.8(b)(3) is no longer required to be verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check PAIR before notifying Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Before notifying the Office of a previously submitted correspondence that appears not to have been received by the Office, applicants are encouraged to check the private Patent Application Information Retrieval (PAIR) System to see if the correspondence has been entered into the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking PAIR can prevent unnecessary petitions or duplicate filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Mail deposit date treated as filing date (37 CFR 1.6(a)(2) and 1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 will be stamped with the date of deposit as 'Express Mail' with the United States Postal Service and considered filed on the date of deposit, even if that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'date-in' on the USPS Express Mail label or other official USPS notation is used. If the USPS deposit date cannot be determined, the Office will use the actual receipt date as the filing date. See 35 U.S.C. 21(a) and 37 CFR 1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO receipt stamping rules and exceptions (37 CFR 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence received in the Patent and Trademark Office is stamped with the date of receipt except: (1) Office not open for filing on Saturdays, Sundays, or Federal holidays (except faxed under (a)(3) or filed electronically under (a)(4)); (2) correspondence filed under §1.10 gets Express Mail date-of-deposit stamp; (3) facsimile transmissions stamped with date the complete transmission is received unless that date is weekend/holiday then next succeeding business day is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand exceptions for facsimile and Express Mail; electronic filings follow different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Mail service and 'date-in' requirement (37 CFR 1.10(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any correspondence delivered by the 'Express Mail Post Office to Addressee' service of the USPS will be considered filed with the USPTO on the date of deposit with the USPS as shown by the 'date-in' on the Express Mail label or other official USPS notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'date-in' must be entered by USPS, not by the applicant. If USPS deposit date cannot be determined, Office uses receipt date. The procedure is limited to USPS Express Mail Post Office to Addressee service and does not apply to International Express Mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Mail deposit practices and label-number placement (37 CFR 1.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence should be deposited directly with an employee of the USPS to ensure the depositor receives a legible copy of the Express Mail mailing label with the 'date-in' clearly marked. The paper(s) or fee(s) should include the 'Express Mail' mailing label number thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositing via drop boxes is at risk of not receiving a legible label/receipt. The mailing label number should be placed on each separate paper or fee transmittal (or cover sheet/transmittal letter itemizing papers). It need not appear on every page of a paper. Parties using drop boxes are advised to maintain a contemporaneous log as backup evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Mail mailing label number requirement and petition consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: As of December 2, 1996, 37 CFR 1.10(b) no longer requires the Express Mail mailing label number be placed on the correspondence prior to mailing for the Office to accord the 'date-in' filing date; however, if the number did not appear on the correspondence as originally filed, relief will not be granted on petition under 37 CFR 1.10(c), (d), (e), (g) or (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve petition rights, place the label number on each separate paper or fee transmittal prior to mailing (directly or via an itemizing cover letter). Failure to do so is considered an avoidable oversight and petitions seeking relief are disfavored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for date-in discrepancy (37 CFR 1.10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(c) applies where there is a discrepancy between the filing date accorded by the Office and the 'date-in' entered by the USPS on the Express Mail mailing label or other official USPS notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.10(c) should be filed promptly after awareness, include a showing that the Express Mail label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing, and include a true copy of the mailing label showing the 'date-in' (or other official USPS notation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for incorrectly entered date-in (37 CFR 1.10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(d) applies where the 'date-in' or other official notation is incorrectly entered by the USPS and a petitioner seeks a filing date as of the actual deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be filed promptly, show that the label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing, and be corroborated by (1) evidence from the USPS (e.g., Corporate Account Mailing Statement) or (2) evidence that came into being after deposit and within one business day of deposit (e.g., contemporaneous log book). Evidence created prior to deposit or more than one business day after deposit is inadequate. Must also show deposit prior to last scheduled pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when correspondence was never received (37 CFR 1.10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(e) applies where correspondence deposited as Express Mail was not received by the Office and petitioner seeks a filing date as of the USPS deposit date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should be filed promptly, include showing that the label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing, include a true copy of the originally deposited correspondence with the label number, copy of any returned postcard receipt, copy of mailing label showing 'date-in' or other USPS notation, and a statement signed by the depositor specifying date/time of deposit and declaring that accompanying copies are true copies of originals. Correspondence must have been mailed with sufficient postage and addressed per 37 CFR 1.1(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for returned/refused/unable-to-deposit due to interruption or emergency (37 CFR 1.10(g)-(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(g) applies where Express Mail was returned by USPS due to an interruption or emergency in Express Mail service; 1.10(h) applies where correspondence was refused by USPS employee due to such interruption/emergency; 1.10(i) applies where attempts to deposit were prevented by a designated interruption/emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be filed promptly, include label numbers placed prior to the attempted mailing, include original correspondence or copies showing the label number, and include a statement by the person who attempted/deposited that establishes the original deposit or attempted deposit (and that copies are true copies). Office may require additional evidence to determine the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standards for petitions (USPS records or contemporaneous log)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where corroboration is required (e.g., 37 CFR 1.10(d)), the showing must be corroborated by evidence from the USPS or evidence that came into being after deposit and within one business day of deposit (such as a log book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable logbook contents: Express Mail number; application number, docket number or file ID; place, date and time of deposit; time of last scheduled pick-up for that date/place; depositor’s initials/signature; date/time of entry in the log. Evidence created prior to deposit or more than one business day after deposit (e.g., affidavits prepared later) will be denied as insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last scheduled pickup requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a filing date as of a requested deposit date, a party must show that the correspondence was deposited as Express Mail prior to the last scheduled pickup on the requested filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of deposit prior to last scheduled pickup must be corroborated by USPS evidence or contemporaneous evidence (log book). 37 CFR 1.10(d)(3) and related petition provisions require this showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require additional evidence (37 CFR 1.10(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require additional evidence to determine if the correspondence was deposited as 'Express Mail' with the USPS on the date in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to supply USPS records or contemporaneous logs and other corroborating materials; absence of sufficient evidence may result in denial of requested filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No waiver for oversights avoidable by ordinary care
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.10 (e.g., failing to place the Express Mail mailing label number on the correspondence) is an oversight that can be avoided by the exercise of reasonable care; requests for waiver of this requirement will not be granted on petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites cases (Honigsbaum v. Lehman; Nitto Chemical; Vincent v. Mossinghoff; Gustafson v. Strange; In re Chicago Historical Antique Automobile Museum) where waivers/refusals to waive were affirmed. Inadvertent omission is not 'unavoidable' or 'extraordinary' for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 133, 37 CFR 1.137(a), 1.183, etc.
